@dev Wrappers over Solidity's uintXX/intXX/bool casting operators with added overflow
 checks.
 Downcasting from uint256/int256 in Solidity does not revert on overflow. This can
 easily result in undesired exploitation or bugs, since developers usually
 assume that overflows raise errors. `SafeCast` restores this intuition by
 reverting the transaction when such an operation overflows.
 Using this library instead of the unchecked operations eliminates an entire
 class of bugs, so it's recommended to use it always.

@notice Sets Hyperlane warp route metadata for a destination chain.
 @dev `_tokenIn` is the asset held by the inbox: the underlying ERC20 for collateral routes,
      the synthetic token (the router itself) for synthetic routes, or `address(0)` for native
      routes. An implemented `token()` must agree with `_tokenIn`; pre-scale HypNative routers
      that predate that selector are accepted only for native input.
      `_remoteScaleNumerator` and `_remoteScaleDenominator` must equal the destination
      TokenRouter's scale getters. Hyperlane first rounds the source-local amount into message
      units using the source router's scale, then rounds message units into destination-local
      units using the inverse remote scale. Both stages are retained so denomination dust
      cannot make the adapter overstate destination output.
      The owner must source the remote scale from the enrolled destination router. It is remote
      chain state and cannot be authenticated by this source-chain contract. The owner must
      also ensure both routers use TokenRouter's standard scale-based amount conversion.
      Custom routers expose the same public selectors, so this invariant cannot be inferred
      from the shared TokenRouter ABI.

@title HyperlaneAdapter
 @author Agustin Aguilar
 @notice Bridge adapter for standard fungible Hyperlane TokenRouter transfers from an inbox
 @dev Hyperlane warp routes deliver the dispatched value without bridge slippage, but source and
      destination routers may express that value in different token denominations. The adapter
      reproduces Hyperlane's source-local -> message -> destination-local scale conversions and
      reports the destination-local amount as `amountOut`. This is the explicit bridge-adapter
      trust boundary: the route's delivery guarantee is the warp route's, enforced by its
      Interchain Security Module rather than by this adapter.
      This adapter supports standard fungible `HypERC20`, `HypERC20Collateral`, and `HypNative`
      routers whose amount conversion is defined by the TokenRouter scale getters. Routers that
      override amount conversion dynamically (for example ERC-4626 share routes), NFT routes,
      and other custom bridges require a dedicated adapter.
      What the adapter must NOT assume is the input side. A warp route with an owner-set
      `feeRecipient` debits `amount + fee` from the caller while still dispatching `amount`, so
      `execute` reports the inbox debit it MEASURES around `transferRemote` rather than the amount
      it requested. Route accounting snapshots the inbox again after the bridge call and reverts
      with `BridgeDebitMismatch` when a declared asset lost more than the quote reports
      (`RouteAccounting._validateBridgeRoute`), so an unreported additive fee cannot escape the
      slippage floor; measuring here is defense in depth, and it is also what keeps those routes
      executable. Modern routers expose the expected debit through `quoteTransferRemote`;
      legacy routers fall back to `quoteGasPayment`. Execution still measures the actual token
      and native debits so the returned quote remains authoritative.
